title: Naturality of the global operator
statement:
Fix the coefficient
conventions and an
admissible cohomological
correspondence $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ whose ordinary leg
$c_2$ is proper, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then the global
operator $T_c(u)$ of [def-trf-global-operator] is natural in
the pair $(u,K)$: a morphism of correspondences
$u\to u'$ over a morphism $K\to K'$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ induces
a commutative square relating $T_c(u)$ and $T_c(u')$.

proof.text: Keep the scheme correspondence $c$ fixed. By [def-trf-correspondence], the two coefficient maps have types $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ and $u':Lc_2^*K'\to Rc_1^!K'$. Write $P=Lc_2^*$, $Q=Rc_1^!$, $H=Rc_{2*}$, $J=Rc_{1!}$, $F=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and $G=R\Gamma_c(C,-)$, with $F$ and $G$ the functors $\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_!$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. In [def-trf-global-operator], let $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to HP$ be the unit of $P\dashv H$ (this is the ordinary pullback adjunction, not the exceptional adjunction of admissibility), and let $\varepsilon:JQ\to\operatorname{id}$ be the exceptional counit supplied by [def-trf-admissibility]. The properness of $c_2$ and the composition law in clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] give the natural comparison $\alpha:FHP\xrightarrow{\sim}GP$; the inverse composition law for $a_Xc_1=a_C$ gives $\beta:GQ\xrightarrow{\sim}FJQ$. These are precisely the comparisons specified in [def-trf-global-operator]. All their domains are the given finite-coefficient constructible domains. Put $p_K=\alpha_K\circ F(\eta_K)$ and $q_K=F(\varepsilon_K)\circ\beta_K$. The five-arrow definition now reads $T_c(u)=q_K\circ G(u)\circ p_K$, and the formula with $K',u'$ defines $T_c(u')$.

source.place: First sentence and the unit, counit, comparison-isomorphism, and functoriality clauses

proof.text: Let $f:K\to K'$ be the stated morphism of coefficient correspondences. Its commuting coefficient square means $Q(f)\circ u=u'\circ P(f)$. Naturality of $\eta$ says $HP(f)\circ\eta_K=\eta_{K'}\circ f$, and naturality of $\alpha$ says $GP(f)\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_{K'}\circ FHP(f)$. Apply $F$ to the first equality and substitute it into the second to obtain $GP(f)\circ p_K=p_{K'}\circ F(f)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ says $f\circ\varepsilon_K=\varepsilon_{K'}\circ JQ(f)$, and naturality of $\beta$ says $FJQ(f)\circ\beta_K=\beta_{K'}\circ GQ(f)$. Apply $F$ to the counit equality and substitute the comparison equality to obtain $F(f)\circ q_K=q_{K'}\circ GQ(f)$. Finally, applying the functor $G$ to the coefficient square gives $GQ(f)\circ G(u)=G(u')\circ GP(f)$. Here $GP(f)$ means $G(P(f))$, and the other juxtaposed functors are interpreted in the same way. These three identities are the naturality squares for the first two, last two, and middle arrows, respectively.

source.place: Each of the five arrows is natural: explicit component equations using the data identified in step 1

proof.text:
Using the three identities of step 2 in order, and associativity of composition, compute
$$\begin{aligned}
F(f)\circ T_c(u)
&=F(f)\circ q_K\circ G(u)\circ p_K\\
&=q_{K'}\circ GQ(f)\circ G(u)\circ p_K\\
&=q_{K'}\circ G(u')\circ GP(f)\circ p_K\\
&=q_{K'}\circ G(u')\circ p_{K'}\circ F(f)
=T_c(u')\circ F(f).
\end{aligned}$$
Since $F(f)=R\Gamma_c(X,f)$, this is exactly the commutative square asserted in the item.
